precepts.text: He will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations among whom he hath scattered us. Again it uses the word nations, explaining that it was Israel being scattered.
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
“And he will scourge us for our iniquities, and will have mercy again, and will gather us out of all nations, among whom he hath scattered us.” Again it uses the word nations, explaining that it was Israel being scattered among them.

The scourge is for our iniquities, but mercy comes again, and the promise is the gathering out of all nations. That is the same gathering Isaiah 11 speaks of, and the same work Christ was sent to begin: bringing the dispersed out from among the Gentiles, where they had been scattered.

precepts.text: Confess him before the Gentiles, ye children of Israel, for he hath scattered us among them; there declare his greatness and extol him before all the living. The same thing Moses said in Deuteronomy 4.
precepts.point: When thou art in tribulation and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord and be obedient, he is a merciful God; he will not forsake thee nor destroy thee, the lake of fire, nor forget the covenant of thy fathers. That is the crown of life of Revelation 2:10.
precepts.why:
“Confess him before the Gentiles, ye children of Israel: for he hath scattered us among them.” Tobit is speaking to the children of Israel, and he tells us plainly where they are: scattered among the Gentiles. The Lord did the scattering, just as Moses said in Deuteronomy 4:27.

“There declare his greatness, and extol him before all the living: for he is our Lord, and he is the God our Father for ever.” There, in those lands where we were scattered, declare his greatness. It is the same thing Moses said in Deuteronomy 4: “But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him”. From thence, from the lands we were taken to, we seek him, and we are seeking him now here in America and finding him.

So Tobit proves both halves of the opened scripture: Israel scattered among the Gentiles, and Israel turning to confess the Lord right there among them. He is our Lord, the God of our fathers for ever, and he has not forgotten the covenant of our fathers.
